import h5py
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from scipy.stats import pearsonr
import statsmodels.api as sm

# Parameters
sessions = range(1, 8)  # Sessions 1–7
pre, post = 0.2, 0.2  # epoch window (s)
baseline_start, baseline_end = -0.1, 0.0
gain_start, gain_end = 0.05, 0.15

all_durations = []
all_amplitudes = []

for ses in sessions:
    meg_file = f'sub-0_ses-{ses}_meg.h5'
    evt_file = f'sub-0_ses-{ses}_events.tsv'

    # Load MEG data
    with h5py.File(meg_file, 'r') as f:
        data = f['data'][:]          # shape: (306, n_times)
        times = f['times'][:]
        # Channel types attribute: decode if bytes
        ch_types_attr = f.attrs['channel_types']
        if isinstance(ch_types_attr, (bytes, bytearray)):
            ch_types_str = ch_types_attr.decode('utf-8')
        else:
            ch_types_str = ch_types_attr
        ch_types = ch_types_str.split(',')
        mag_inds = [i for i, t in enumerate(ch_types) if t == 'mag']

    # Load events
    df = pd.read_csv(evt_file, sep='\t')
    df_ph = df[df['kind'] == 'phoneme'][['timemeg', 'duration']].dropna()

    for t0, dur in zip(df_ph['timemeg'], df_ph['duration']):
        # Skip if epoch window exceeds data bounds
        if t0 < pre or t0 > times[-1] - post:
            continue
        # Determine sample indices for epoch and windows
        start_idx = np.searchsorted(times, t0 - pre)
        end_idx = np.searchsorted(times, t0 + post)
        b0 = np.searchsorted(times, t0 + baseline_start)
        b1 = np.searchsorted(times, t0 + baseline_end)
        g0 = np.searchsorted(times, t0 + gain_start)
        g1 = np.searchsorted(times, t0 + gain_end)

        epoch = data[mag_inds, start_idx:end_idx]
        baseline = data[mag_inds, b0:b1]
        # Baseline correction
        baseline_mean = baseline.mean(axis=1, keepdims=True)
        epoch_corr = epoch - baseline_mean

        # Relative gain window indices
        rel_g0 = g0 - start_idx
        rel_g1 = g1 - start_idx
        if rel_g0 < 0 or rel_g1 > epoch_corr.shape[1]:
            continue
        # Compute mean amplitude over channels and time window
        amp = epoch_corr[:, rel_g0:rel_g1].mean()
        all_durations.append(dur)
        all_amplitudes.append(amp)

# Convert to NumPy arrays
durations = np.array(all_durations)
amplitudes = np.array(all_amplitudes)

# Pearson correlation
r, p_corr = pearsonr(durations, amplitudes)
print(f"Pearson correlation: r = {r:.3f}, p = {p_corr:.3e}")

# Linear regression (amplitude ~ duration)
X = sm.add_constant(durations)
model = sm.OLS(amplitudes, X).fit()
print(model.summary())

# Plot scatter with regression line
plt.figure(figsize=(8, 6))
plt.scatter(durations, amplitudes, alpha=0.4, label='Trials')
# Regression line
d_range = np.linspace(durations.min(), durations.max(), 100)
intercept, slope = model.params
line = intercept + slope * d_range
plt.plot(d_range, line, color='red', label='Linear fit')
plt.xlabel('Phoneme duration (s)')
plt.ylabel('Evoked amplitude (T)')
plt.title('Phoneme duration vs. early-evoked amplitude (magnetometers)')
plt.legend()
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
